correctness.rationale: The uniform full-sphere midpoint/tangent/half-angle disintegration has Jacobian sin(2t)dt, and hemisphere conditioning by a probability 1/4 gives joint density 1/(2pi^2) restricted to w<q(z,phi). The exact trigonometric integral 2pi/z gives midpoint density z/pi, whose spherical-area Jacobian produces uniform planar area. The conditional Cauchy direction and uniform w follow by division; an independent spherical-lune argument gives f_Delta=(1-delta/pi)sin(delta). Dimension uniqueness follows from pole density 4/surface(S^{d-1}) compared with 1/volume(B^{d-1}), and strict increase of the gamma quotient. A standalone numerical check ran successfully with 660000 directly sampled endpoint pairs and 340000 independently reconstructed pairs; numerical sampling is not a substitute for proof.
